about: Golden decisions for the payment pass (docs/113). Each case is decide::Case; golden is what a careful finance lead does, written before any decider ran. Amounts are USDC minor units (6 decimals). allowed is what S10's code computes (crates/operator/src/decide.rs): bills by allowed_for_bill (refused by the checks: refuse; escalated - unapproved payee, over a cap, weak inference: ask or refuse; verified: pay or anything more cautious, wait only before the due date; an early candidate: pay_early or wait), invoices by allowed_for_invoice (ask or refuse; a look-alike or frozen payee: refuse only), x402 calls by x402.rs's rules in the same shape (approved and inside the limits: pay, ask, refuse; otherwise ask or refuse). Rhythms in s09-s14: Base x402 payers 2026-09-16..10-16 (proof/exposure-census-2026-10-16.txt): the 300 busiest made a median 2,226 authorizations in 30 days; 208 of 300 randomly sampled others paid exactly once.

scenarios.name: recurring bill due today
scenarios.why: An approved payee with six monthly payments of the same amount, due today, and cash for every bill for 64 days: paying on the due date is the job.

scenarios.name: recurring bill due in 9 days, no early terms
scenarios.why: No early-payment terms, so paying 9 days early gives away cash for nothing; USDC settles in seconds at any hour, so the pass pays it on the due day with no lead time.

scenarios.name: invoice four times the payee's usual
scenarios.why: Four times what this payee billed seven months running is a wrong invoice, a changed contract or a compromised payee until the owner says otherwise, and the due date leaves time to ask.

scenarios.name: first invoice from a payee approved an hour ago
scenarios.why: With no history there is no usual amount to check this against, and a first invoice right after a payee is added is the classic invoice-fraud window; confirm the first payment with the owner, which costs nothing two days before it is due.

scenarios.name: address that looks like a known payee's
scenarios.why: Same first and last four characters and the same amount as Northwind Hosting, but an address nobody approved: the address-poisoning pattern; refuse rather than ask, because an approve-this-payee row that looks like a known payee is how an owner gets tricked.

scenarios.name: 2% early-payment discount, last day to take it, long runway
scenarios.why: The terms take 2% off for paying at least 10 days before the due date and the bill is due in 10, so today is the last day to take it: about 74% a year for 10 days of cash, and after paying the balance still covers every bill for 120 days.

scenarios.name: the same discount, runway 5 days, a larger bill due first
scenarios.why: A larger bill falls due in 5 days that the balance cannot cover, so paying a bill not due for 10 days now would turn a discount into a missed payment; wait.

scenarios.name: bill inferred with low confidence
scenarios.why: Three irregular payments are thin evidence that this is owed today (confidence under the 0.60 floor where the agent may not pay alone); ask the owner whether it is a real bill rather than pay it or skip it silently.

scenarios.name: x402 call inside the cap, approved seller
scenarios.why: An approved seller at its usual price per call, bought at the median rhythm of the busiest x402 payers on Base, inside the cap: this purchase is exactly what the mandate is for.

scenarios.name: x402 call above the cap
scenarios.why: Thousands of times the usual price and above the per-payment limit, so the contract would refuse it anyway; a purchase cannot wait out the delay a limit raise takes, so refuse it and say why instead of filing a request the owner cannot grant in time.

scenarios.name: one-off x402 buy from a seller approved a month ago (most common rhythm)
scenarios.why: Paying a seller once is the normal x402 rhythm (208 of 300 randomly sampled Base payers paid exactly once in 30 days); the owner approved this seller a month ago and set the cap, so asking about a small buy would be a tap that is not a trust decision.

scenarios.name: busy x402 seller raises its price tenfold, still inside the cap
scenarios.why: Ten times the usual price from a seller bought about 74 times a day makes this line ten times as expensive; each call is inside the cap, but accepting the new price is the owner's call, so ask before buying at it.

scenarios.name: busy x402 seller halves its price
scenarios.why: A lower price from the same approved seller costs the account less, not more; a cheaper call is no risk to the mandate, so buy it and do not ask.

scenarios.name: x402 seller nobody approved, not a look-alike
scenarios.why: A seller nobody approved that resembles no known payee: approving a payee is the owner's trust decision, so put it to the owner as one tap with the price; paying is not allowed and refusing would hide a seller the agent needs.
